memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Israelites captured the Midianite women and children and took all the Midianite herds, flocks and goods as plunder. They burned all the towns where the Midianites had settled, as well as all their camps. They took all the plunder and spoils, including the people and animals, and brought the captives, spoils and plunder to Moses and Eleazar the priest and the Israelite assembly at their camp on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan across from Jericho. - Num 31:10-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The soldiers returned with everything — captives, animals, goods — and brought it all to Moses, Eleazar, and the whole assembly. On the surface it looks like a complete victory. But the next verses will reveal that the army had spared the very Midianite women who had led Israel into sin at Peor. The problem that started this whole judgment had been carried right back into the camp.

This is a striking picture of how sin can slip back in when we are not watchful, even in the middle of what looks like obedience. We can win a battle in one area of life while quietly leaving open the very door that caused the trouble in the first place. Victory is not just about what we conquer; it is about what we refuse to bring home with us.

Jesus taught us to deal ruthlessly with sin — to cut off whatever causes us to stumble (Matt 5:29-30). He was not talking about harming people, but about the seriousness with which we should treat temptation. The good news is that we do not fight this battle in our own strength. The Spirit within us gives us power to say no to what once controlled us (Rom 8:13). Real freedom is not just escaping sin's penalty but being kept from its return.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there an old temptation you have "brought back into camp" instead of leaving behind?
2. What door in your life needs to be firmly shut?
3. How can the Spirit help you guard against sin's quiet return?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for the victories You give, but guard me from carrying old sins back into my heart. By Your Spirit, help me shut every door that leads me away from You. Amen.
